questions.q: According to this lesson, how is the Microsoft Purview portal organized?
options: As one shared portal covering several distinct solution families, including Data Governance, Data Security, and Risk & Compliance
As entirely separate, unrelated products with no shared portal at all
Purview only offers data governance features — nothing else exists in the portal
Every solution in Purview requires a completely separate login and URL
questions.explain: The Purview portal's home page and Solutions page group a wide set of solutions together, with data governance (this course's focus) as just one of several families.

questions.q: Which four sections does the Purview Solutions page group its offerings into?
options: Core, Risk & Compliance, Data Governance, and Data Security
Basic, Standard, Premium, and Enterprise
Windows, Azure, Microsoft 365, and Dynamics
Free, Trial, Paid, and Legacy
questions.explain: The Solutions page organizes everything into Core (shared setup), Risk & Compliance, Data Governance, and Data Security sections.

questions.q: What does the Compliance posture status card on the Purview portal home page actually report?
options: An assessment-tracking score from a separate solution called Compliance Manager
This course's own certification exam score
A direct legal ruling on whether the organization is compliant with GDPR
The number of data governance lessons completed by the user
questions.explain: The card surfaces a percentage score from Compliance Manager reflecting progress toward completing regulatory assessments — it's a real score from a real solution, but a separate one from this course's governance content.

questions.q: Per this lesson, who is actually qualified to determine whether an organization's data handling satisfies a regulation like GDPR or HIPAA?
options: Qualified legal and compliance professionals who know that organization's full context
Any dashboard score above 80%, automatically
This course, based on the Compliance posture status card alone
Whoever has the Data source admin role in Purview
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that regulatory compliance is a legal determination made by qualified professionals with full context — not something a score, dashboard, or course can determine on its own.

questions.q: Why does this course stop short of teaching Purview's compliance solutions like Data Loss Prevention and eDiscovery in depth?
options: Teaching them properly requires teaching the regulatory context they support, which is outside this course's data-governance scope
Those solutions don't actually exist in Microsoft Purview
They are identical to the Data Map and Data Catalog features already taught
Microsoft has discontinued all of those solutions
questions.explain: Compliance solutions like DLP, Information Protection, eDiscovery, and Records Management are real, substantial products whose proper use depends on regulatory context — each deep enough to be its own course, and outside this course's data-governance scope.
